claims.text: The onset of phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles is governed by surface segregation of Cu.
Increasing temperature causes Cu to diffuse toward and concentrate at the nanoparticle surface.
Cu surface enrichment lowers the local melting point.
A Cu-rich surface layer melts before the nanoparticle core.
The surface-initiated melt front propagates inward.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are fully solid and compositionally homogeneous.
The lower melting point of Cu drives its surface segregation at elevated temperature.
The molten surface shell facilitates further atomic rearrangement.
Surface-layer melting leads to progressive melting of the nanoparticle.
Heated equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will exhibit surface melting accompanied by measurable Cu surface enrichment.
Reducing the Cu content will delay or reduce the onset of surface melting relative to equiatomic particles.
The proposed mechanism is relevant specifically to nanoscale HEA particles under inert conditions.
Bulk material may exhibit different thermal behavior from the nanoparticles.
Oxidizing environments may produce behavior different from that under inert conditions.
The temperature of significant Cu segregation and surface melting may vary with particle size.
The segregation temperature and inward melt-front rate may vary with heating rate and compositional deviations.

contradictions.description: The baseline says a homogeneous nanoparticle would not show early surface melting or Cu gradients under similar heating, whereas the predicted outcome says the equiatomic nanoparticle will show both. It is unclear whether the baseline is merely the pre-heating state or a distinct heated control.
